description.fun: Chingling bounces from place to place, and the red orb in its mouth rings like a bell with every hop. It can vibrate that orb to make long, high-pitched cries, sometimes too high for people to hear yet still strong enough to give them a headache, rather like a wailing toddler. It's the lightest of all baby Pokémon.
description.guide: A Psychic-type baby Pokémon introduced in Generation 4, a generation after Chimecho, based on the suzu bells of Shinto shrines. It evolves into Chimecho when levelled up with high friendship at night.
description.tagline: A jingle-bell baby that rings with every hop

description.fun: Chimecho is shaped like a fūrin, a Japanese glass wind chime, and it hangs from tree branches or the eaves of buildings by the sucker on its head. Its hollow body amplifies the faint sound of the wind into ultrasonic waves that drive off attackers, and it uses seven different echoing cries to talk to others. It rides the wind to fly and gets livelier in hot weather.
description.guide: A Psychic-type Pokémon based on a Japanese glass wind chime, active at night in grasslands and woods. It evolves from Chingling with high friendship at night and can Mega Evolve with the Chimechite.
description.tagline: A living wind chime that speaks in seven echoing cries

description.fun: Mega Chimecho, added in the Mega Dimension DLC for Legends: Z-A, grows a Chingling-shaped ornament hung with six smaller Chimecho that flutter even when there's no wind. Its bright cries soothe Trainers and are said to purify evil spirits, but its sonic blasts can leave foes so dazed they forget who they are. It may be based on the ringed staff carried by Buddhist monks.

note.text: Chingling is a baby Pokémon added in Generation 4, a generation after Chimecho. From Generation 4 to 8, a Chimecho had to hold a Pure Incense for its Egg to hatch into Chingling.
